output.review_comment:
Two of the changes look right. The negative-quantity `ValueError` and the `quantity == 0` early return match the docstring. Switching to `(top - first + 1)` also looks like the real bug fix, since it treats tier bounds as inclusive. For example, tier 1–10 is 10 units, not 9.

The new "volume pricing" branch is the problem. When the quantity reaches the open-ended last tier, it charges every unit at the last tier's price, and that isn't graduated pricing. Graduated pricing charges each unit at the rate of the tier it falls in. This branch contradicts the function's name, and it makes the price jump sharply at the last tier's threshold: buying one more unit can make the whole order much cheaper. It reads like a special case added to make one failing test pass, not something that follows from the spec.

Please remove this branch and check whether the tests pass with only the inclusive-bound fix and the input validation. If a test still fails, it probably points to another off-by-one or tier-boundary problem that needs its own fix. If the pricing team really wants volume pricing above some threshold, that should be written into the docstring and spec explicitly, not quietly added to a function named `graduated_price_cents`. The PR also has no description. Please add one that explains the root cause.
